newsitem.title: NEPAL: Nepal orders re-vote after violent elections.
newsitem.headline: Nepal orders re-vote after violent elections.

text.p: Nepal will hold new polls in hundreds of centres where local elections were cancelled after violence in which six people died, officials said on Wednesday.
"We have asked the local returning officers to complete the repolling as soon as possible," an Election Commission spokesman told Reuters.
Voting in 437 polling stations out of 2,079 centres where elections were held on Monday, was cancelled because of clashes between rival political groups.
"It (the cancellation) was mostly due to violence, and in some cases polling could not be held due to heavy rains," said Purushottam Dhakal, Election Commission spokesman.

Elections for nearly 190,000 representatives in 4,000 village committees and 58 municipalities for a five-year term were held in two phases on May 17 and May 26. These bodies are the Himalayan kingdom's equivalent of local self governments.

Latest results from the May 17 first phase elections showed the communist Unified Marxist-Leninist (UML) party, part of the ruling coalition, had won in more than 34,000 places while the opposition Nepali Congress party won 23,500 places.
Prime Minister Lokendra Bahadur Chand's Rastriya Prajatantra Party (RPP) was trailing in 9,000 seats.
Full results are expected after two weeks.
